results.title: DigitalOcean GPU Droplets Review, Pricing & Alternatives | Saaskly
highlights:
## What it costs

 Prices are shown in US dollars to a UK visitor, with VAT not stated. All figures read on 22 September 2026.

 An NVIDIA HGX H100 with 80 GB is $4.41 per GPU-hour on demand, which is about $3,219 a month at 730 hours. Commit for 12 months and the same card is $3.26 an hour, roughly $2,380 a month, so the on-demand rate carries a 35 per cent premium. The GPU arrives in a Droplet with 20 vCPU, 240 GiB of RAM, a 720 GiB NVMe boot disk and a 5 TiB NVMe scratch disk, and you can buy one GPU or eight. Eight H100s on demand is $35.28 an hour, about $25,754 a month. An H200 is $4.47 an hour on demand and $3.40 reserved, an AMD MI300X is $2.59 and $1.91, an MI325X is $3.80 and $2.88. The cheapest card of any kind is the RTX 4000 Ada with 20 GB at $0.76 an hour, about $555 a month, in a smaller Droplet with 8 vCPU and 32 GiB of RAM. An L40S or an RTX 6000 Ada is $1.57. Spot capacity exists on the newest parts, but the published spot rates for B300 at $11.19 and MI355X at $4.50 sit above the equivalent on-demand and reserved rates, which contradicts DigitalOcean's own documentation that spot is always at or below on demand.

...

Signup is self-serve with a card, and a GPU Droplet can in principle be launched the same day. What stands in the way is the account limit. DigitalOcean does not publish the default GPU Droplet quota for a new account, and the route to raise it is a request in the control panel under Settings and Profile, or a support ticket, rather than an automatic increase. September 2026 Trustpilot reviews describe a new account restricted from the larger advertised Droplets despite valid payment, with access said to require months of billing history or up to $1,000 prepaid, and a DigitalOcean community question from November 2025 shows a GPU limit increase request going unanswered on the page. Bare Metal GPUs are a different purchase entirely: 8x H100, 8x H200 or 8x MI300X nodes with dual Xeon Platinum CPUs, 2,048 GiB of RAM, 61.44 TiB of NVMe and RDMA interconnect up to 3.2 Tbps, but they are "provisioned via contract with DigitalOcean sales (not on-demand)", with no public price.

results.title: Best GPU Cloud for UK Business 2026: OVHcloud Wins
highlights:
DigitalOcean GPU Droplets (3.8) is the trusted name with the wrong map. The H100 is $4.41 an hour on demand and $3.26 on a published 12-month reservation, a 35% gap you can take without a sales call; an eight-GPU node is $35.28 an hour; the RTX 4000 Ada starts at $0.76. Single-GPU plans include 10,000 GiB of transfer with a cent-a-gigabyte overage, managed Kubernetes takes GPU node pools, and there is an official Terraform provider, the doctl CLI and a published MCP server, though that server is built around App Platform. Trustpilot is 4.5 on 2,572 uninvited reviews, the best record of any US provider here. But London has no GPU Droplets of any kind; Amsterdam is the only EU GPU site and carries H100 only. A stopped GPU Droplet bills in full with no monthly cap, the GPU SLA is 99% against 99.99% for CPU Droplets and a claim needs written notice within 24 hours, the new-account GPU limit is unpublished and lifted by request, and the bare-metal GPU nodes are sales-only. Not yet tested by Saaskly.

results.title: DigitalOcean GPU Droplets 怎么选？H100、H200、L40S 价格和关机计费讲清楚 | 智机玄同
results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月9日 4 分钟阅读
highlights:
智机玄同发布于 2026年10月9日 4 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月9日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

...

## 当前公开价格

截至 2026-10-09，DigitalOcean 官方 GPU Droplet 价格包括：

- NVIDIA L40S 48GB：$1.57 / 小时
- NVIDIA H100 80GB：$4.41 / 小时
- NVIDIA H200 141GB：$4.47 / 小时

还有 RTX 4000 Ada、RTX 6000 Ada、AMD MI300X、MI325X 等型号。

这些数字是 On-Demand GPU Droplet 当前公开价格，不是长期合约价。

## 实际按秒计费

虽然官网用“每小时”展示，GPU Droplet 实际按秒计费。

当前规则是：

- 最低计费 60 秒；
- 或最低 $0.01；
- 两者取较高者。

所以跑 20 分钟任务，不需要按整小时买。

这点对短测试比较友好。

## 但关机以后还会收费

这是 DigitalOcean 最容易踩的坑。

官方文档明确说明：

GPU Droplet powered off 以后仍然继续计费。

因为 GPU、CPU、RAM 和其他资源仍然保留给你。

真正停止实例费用，需要：

Destroy Droplet。

所以它的逻辑和一些“Stop GPU 就停止计算费”的平台不同。

如果只是离开一晚，不要想当然地以为按下 Power Off 后账单就停止。

results.title: Where to get H100 GPUs without long-term a commitment - DEV Community
results.author: DigitalOcean
highlights:
You can get H100 GPUs without a contract from DigitalOcean GPU Droplets. Create one from the console or API, pay per second, and destroy it when the job ends. Commitments only pay off once your usage is steady.

Key takeaways:

- On-demand H100 GPU Droplets pricing starts at \$4.41 per GPU per hour (as of October 2026), billed per second, with no term. 
- A 12-month reserved H100 rate is lower (\$3.26 per GPU per hour), but that is the commitment you are avoiding. 
- Powering off does not stop billing. Destroying the Droplet does.

## What on-demand H100 access looks like 

H100 GPU Droplets come with one GPU (80 GB of GPU memory, 20 vCPUs, 240 GiB of RAM) or eight (640 GB of GPU memory, 160 vCPUs, 1,920 GiB of RAM), at \$35.28 per hour for the eight-GPU size. They are available in New York (NYC2), Amsterdam (AMS3), and Toronto (TOR1). Billing is per second with a 60-second or \$0.01 minimum, whichever is higher.

results.title: DigitalOcean vs Together AI for AI Inference in 2026
results.author: Maddy Osman
highlights:
Pricing and feature information in this article are based on publicly available documentation as of September 2026 and may vary by region and workload. For the most current pricing and availability, please refer to each provider’s official documentation.

...

## Pricing

Both DigitalOcean and Together AI bill primarily per token for serverless traffic, but there are several differences to be aware of in terms of how they approach pricing.

Pricing and product information below correct as of September 2026, and subject to change.

| Point of comparison | DigitalOcean | Together AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serverless tokens | ~0.10–1.05+/1M input tokens for DO-hosted models; proxied OpenAI/Anthropic bill at each provider’s list rates | ~0.03–4.50/1M tokens, by model |
| Dedicated inference | From 2.59/GPU-hour(AMDMI300X) | ~3.99–$6.49/GPU-hour for H100, by commitment |
| GPU clusters | Not a separate product—dedicated GPU Droplets cover this | Rentable clusters from ~$3.49+/hour on-demand, billed separately |
| Fine-tuning | Included via BYOM deployment, no separate meter | Billed per training token, plus a separate post-training hosting bill |
| Batch discount | Up to 50% off on OpenAI and Anthropic models | ~50% off serverless batch jobs |
| Billing structure | One bill across inference, databases, storage, and compute | Four separately-metered products (serverless, dedicated, clusters, fine-tuning), each with its own rate card |

results.title: Can't Get a GPU VM? AWS vs Azure vs Google Cloud vs DigitalOcean in 2026 | FogerLogTech
results.author: Mehmood
highlights:
## DigitalOcean GPU Droplets

DigitalOcean's list is shorter but simple: L40S ($1.57 an hour), RTX 4000 Ada ($0.76), RTX 6000 Ada ($1.57), H100 ($4.41 per GPU) and H200 ($4.47 per GPU), plus AMD Instinct. H100 and H200 Droplets come as one or eight GPUs; an H100 Droplet has 20 vCPUs, 240 GiB RAM, 720 GiB boot NVMe and 5 TiB scratch NVMe. I found no A100 or L4.

Availability is the catch. DigitalOcean's availability page (last verified 10 August 2026) shows on-demand H100 in New York (NYC2), Amsterdam (AMS3) and Toronto (TOR1), H200 in NYC2 and Atlanta (ATL1), and L40S in TOR1 only. GPU Droplet limits are 0 on Tier 1, then 1, 2, 4 and 16 on Tiers 2 to 5.

Billing is per second, and powered-off GPU Droplets are still billed. The pages disagree on the minimum: the GPU Droplets pricing page says five minutes, the Droplet pricing documentation 60 seconds. Check before relying on short jobs.
